'''Annette Huber-Klawitter''' (née Huber, born 23 May 1967) is a German [[mathematician]] at the [[University of Freiburg]]. Her research interests includes [[algebraic geometry]], in particular the [[Special values of L-functions|Bloch–Kato conjectures]].

== Early life and education ==
Annette Huber-Klawitter was born on 23 May 1967 in [[Frankfurt am Main]]. Between 1984 and 1986, she won the ''Bundeswettbewerb Mathematik'', a national mathematics competition, three times in a row. <ref>{{cite web|url = https://idw-online.de/de/news99309|title=Eine Million für "reine Mathematik"}}</ref>

She began her academic career at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] and obtained her [[doctorate]] from the [[University of Münster]] in 1994. Her PhD dissertation was titled ''Realisierung von gemischten Motiven in derivierten Kategorien und ihre Kohomologie'' ("Realisation of mixed motives in derived categories and their cohomologies") and completed under the supervision of [[Christopher Deninger]].<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=83705}}</ref> From 1995 to 1996, she spent two years as a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name = leopoldina></ref>

== Career ==
In 1995, Huber-Klawitter won the [[Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Prize]],<ref name = leopoldina></ref> and in 1996, she won an [[EMS Prize]].

She completed her Habilitation in 1999 at the [[University of Münster]]. In 2000, she became a professor of pure mathematics at the [[University of Leipzig]]. Since 2008, she is the chair of [[Number Theory]] at the [[University of Freiburg]].

She was an invited speaker at the 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Beijing]].<ref>''Equivariant Bloch-Kato conjecture and non-abelian Iwasawa Main Conjecture'', with Guido Kings.</ref> 

In 2008, she was elected a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref name = leopoldina>{{cite web |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/annette-huber-klawitter/|title=Anette Huber-Klawitter at www.leopoldina.org}}</ref> In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-21.</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* ''Mixed Motives and their realization in derived categories'', [[Lecture Notes in Mathematics|Lecture notes in Mathematics]] 1604, Springer 1995
* with J. Wildeshaus: ''Classical motivic polylogarithm according to Beilinson and Deligne.'' [[Documenta Mathematica|Doc. Math.]] 3 (1998), 27–133
* with [[Guido Kings]]: ''Degeneration of l-adic Eisenstein classes and of the elliptic polylog.'' [[Inventiones Mathematicae|Invent. Math.]] 135 (1999), no. 3, 545–594.
*''Was wir über Gleichungen vom Grad 3 (nicht) wissen: Elliptische Kurven und die Vermutung von Birch und Swinnerton-Dyer'', in ''Facettenreiche Mathematik. Einblicke in die moderne mathematische Forschung für alle, die mehr von Mathematik verstehen wollen'', Vieweg/Teubner 2011, S. 215–236
*with [[:de:Stefan Müller-Stach]]: ''Periods and Nori motives'', Springer, [[Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete]], 2017
